title: Excel Entertainment and AA Films Board Malayalam Vampire Thriller for Toronto Midnight Madness
excerpt: Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani's production house teams up with AA Films to bring the pan-Indian horror film to one of TIFF's most coveted genre sections.
body:
• Excel Entertainment and AA Films have boarded 'Half: The Chronicles of Two Half-Blooded Vampires,' a Malayalam vampire thriller selected for TIFF's Midnight Madness programme.
  • Directed by Samjad and produced by Fragrant Nature Film Creations, the film stars Amala Paul, Ranjith Sajeev, and Aiswarya Raj, with veteran actor Abbas marking his return to cinema.
  • The film is being positioned as a pan-Indian release in five languages — Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, and Kannada.
  • Action choreography by Very Tri Yulisman, known for Hollywood productions, gives the film a global production pedigree.

Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani's Excel Entertainment has teamed up with AA Films to board Half: The Chronicles of Two Half-Blooded Vampires, a Malayalam-language vampire thriller that has been selected for the Toronto International Film Festival's prestigious Midnight Madness section, according to Variety.

The deal marks a notable push by one of Bollywood's most prominent production houses into south Indian genre cinema, bringing its distribution muscle to a film conceived as a large-scale, pan-Indian spectacle.

A Genre Film With National Ambitions

Directed by Samjad, who made his debut with the well-received Golam, Half is rooted in vampire mythology and explores themes of identity, duality, survival, and vengeance. The film is produced by Anne Sajeev and Sajeev PK under the Fragrant Nature Film Creations banner.

Ranjith Sajeev stars as one of two half-blooded vampires at the centre of the story, alongside Aiswarya Raj in the other central role. Amala Paul plays a pivotal part, while veteran South Indian actor Abbas returns to cinema after a long hiatus — a casting choice that has generated considerable anticipation among fans of Tamil and Malayalam film.

Hollywood-Grade Technical Crew

The production has assembled a crew that bridges Indian and international filmmaking. Action choreography is handled by Very Tri Yulisman, whose credits span major Hollywood productions, lending Half a distinctive global edge in its fight sequences and set pieces.

Behind the camera, the team includes National Award-winning editor Mahesh Bhuvanend, known for his work on Aattam, Vela, and Madhuram. Music is composed by Midhun Mukundan, whose scores for Rorschach and Abraham Ozler earned wide acclaim. Cinematography is by Pappinu, and sound design comes from National Award-winner Vishnu Govind, recognised for Malik, Unda, and Ishq.

Production designer Mohandas, whose portfolio includes 2018, Ayyappanum Koshiyum, and Lucifer, completes what the makers are calling one of Malayalam cinema's most ambitious technical ensembles.

"Excel's track record at TIFF also helps."

Why TIFF's Midnight Madness Matters

The Midnight Madness section at TIFF is one of the festival circuit's most sought-after slots for genre films. Past selections have launched international careers and generated cult followings. For Half, a berth in the programme provides international exposure that few Indian genre films receive.

Excel Entertainment's involvement is significant. The company, founded by Akhtar and Sidhwani, has been behind some of Indian cinema's most commercially successful films, from Dil Chahta Hai to the Don franchise and Mirzapur. Its partnership with AA Films — which has previously handled Hindi distribution for south Indian blockbusters including KGF: Chapter 2 — signals strong commercial intent behind the release.

Diaspora Audiences in Focus

The five-language release strategy positions Half to reach diaspora audiences across multiple linguistic communities. Indian horror and genre films have historically found enthusiastic reception among overseas audiences, particularly in North America and the UK, where festival screenings can build word-of-mouth ahead of theatrical runs.

Excel's track record at TIFF also helps. The company's Boong premiered at the 2024 festival and went on to win at BAFTA, returning to theatres with a wider release in 2026.

What's Next

The Toronto International Film Festival runs in September. Half is expected to use its Midnight Madness premiere as a launchpad for global distribution talks while building anticipation for its theatrical release across India's five major language markets.
